page.layout: Two engraved coin medallions at the top, side by side, with no text block of their own. Below them one column of running text. At the foot, a signature at the right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: ZENO Constantinopoli imperat anno mundi 4437. à Christo nato 475. fuit ex Isauris Ciliciæ, obscuri sanguinis, facie deformis, moribus tyrannus, ut Isaurũ agnoscas. Hic Theodoricum Ostrogothorum Regẽ cum unicè diligeret, Cõsulem fecit, ac in Italiam aduersus Odoacrẽ misit: occurrẽtem Odoacrem Theodoricus prælio vicit, fugauit: fugiẽs Odoacer, intra mœnia vrbis non admissus, citissimè Rauẽnam cõtendit. triennium ibi obsessus, tãdémque à Theodorico in fidem receptus, contra fidem truculeter excarnificatur. Pellitur regno Zeno à Basilisco factione vxoris Augustæ, cùm in Isauriam cõcesisset maritus Imperator: non multò pòst reuersus Zeno Basiliscũ expulit, quẽ vnà cum filio inedia mori coëgit. Sunt qui viuum adhuc inclusum ab vxore sepulchro tradant. Hoc principe incendium odeò graue fuit, ut præter maximã vrbis partem conflagratam, centum & viginti librorum millia combusta sint: inter quæ & Homeri poëma, intestino draconis 120. pedũ, aureis literis descriptum. Pom. Læt.Pau.Diac.lib.6.Egna.lib.2.

ARIADNA, supradicti Zenonis uxor, fratrem Basiliscum Imperatorem fecit, filiúmque eius Cæsarem, absente quidem viro suo, qui rediés[?] supplicium de patre & filio sumpsit, uti iam dictum est. Bap.Egna.lib.2.Romanorum Principum.

page.notes: The two engraved medallions above the text show, on the left, a laureate bust in profile with a legend around the rim reading approximately "IMP ZENONVS P AVG"; on the right, a draped female bust with a legend reading approximately "ARIADNA ZENO IMP AVG". The rim legends are part of the engraving and are not transcribed as text; the readings are my best reading of the rims and are uncertain. Word "rediés" in the second paragraph: the accent or letter form is doubtful. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The first paragraph's marginal abbreviations are kept as printed.
